newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude boosted late session by short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude boosted late session by short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude rebounded from early losses Tuesday afternoon on a late bout of short covering as traders squared positions ahead of weekly oil inventory data.
"I think it's a matter of technical factors and short covering ahead of the stats," said a New York crude dealer.
At 1458 EST, April crude was up 55 cents a barrel at $20.80, a session high, after falling 17 cents to $20.08 earlier.
"We fell earlier and we were able to hold above $20.00, so that was a very good technical sign," said a dealer.
Spot crude was also able to rebound from its lows Monday after dipping below $20.00 for the first time in eight months.
April gasoline was up 1.23 cents at 63.00 cents a gallon while April heating oil was up 0.77 cent a gallon at 53.95 cents.

Prompt heating oil earlier held key trendline support drawn from the spot low in April 1995. Most traders expect this evening's weekly oil inventory report by the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a slight build in gasoline stocks, but refiner de-stocking and strong demand could lead to a surprise decline.

Higher imports were seen boosting crude stocks by up to four million barrels. Distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, were seen showing a seasonal draw of one to to two million barrels.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
